Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

prove verb

show to be true

also proof, demonstrate, prove that, prove someone wrong, that proves it

classical

Caes. BG 1.3.5: perfacile factū esse illīs probat
Cic. Tusc. 5.1: difficile est probātū
Traupman 366

probō, probāre, probāvī, probātum

verb, first conjugation: aliquid alicui probāre, or with an accusative and infinitive

prove, show (a thing to someone)

Properly “make good, make acceptable”: what is proved to someone is made credible to him, and the same verb is “approve” (Lewis & Short). “This proves that …” is documentō est (Traupman 366; see evidence).

Other words

  • dēmōnstrō, dēmōnstrāre, dēmōnstrāvī, dēmōnstrātum — show, demonstrate, prove

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.4.1: dēmōnstrāvit mē ā tē plūrimī fierī

    Literally “point out”: to show by argument or description (Lewis & Short).

  • convincō, convincere, convīcī, convictum — prove (someone) wrong or guilty; prove (a thing) beyond question

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.8: quō mē teste convincās?; Traupman 195, 311

    Of persons, to convict of a fault or an error, the charge in the genitive; of things, to show a thing false or wrong beyond doubt (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Perfacile factū esse illīs probat cōnāta perficere

    He proves to them that it would be very easy to carry out their plansCaes. BG 1.3.5

  • quod etsī difficile est probātū propter tam varia et tam multa tormenta fortūnae

    and though this is hard to prove, because of fortune’s many and various tormentsCic. Tusc. 5.1

  • sed quid oppōnās tandem, sī negem mē umquam ad tē istās litterās mīsisse? quō mē teste convincās?

    But what will you set against it, if I deny ever having sent you that letter? With what witness will you prove me wrong?Cic. Phil. 2.8

See also evidence, show, prove, true, explain.
